item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is the less invasive and better-tested patch, but neither candidate satisfies the frozen contract and neither should merge as-is.","reasons":["A directly verifies retrying buffered multipart data from a non-seekable io.MultiReader; B’s Upload retry test uses an os.File and therefore does not specifically cover streamed, non-replayable source content.","A leaves the existing FilesOption constructors untouched, while B introduces FilesRequestOption and changes the return types and implementation of WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions.","A’s seekable-body retry support avoids B’s extra SeekEnd operation and Content-Length inference, which broaden behavior and rely on the incorrect assumption that a failed seek leaves the offset unchanged.","A is somewhat easier to repair toward the contract because it has less shared option-system churn."],"risks_a":["Upload has the wrong signature: it accepts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required ...FilesOption.","Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating Add’s request and response behavior.","It adds prohibited association APIs and extends multipartbody with NewForm instead of simply reusing multipartbody.NewFile as required, creating unnecessary scope and API surface. Existing FilesOption values cannot configure Upload normally, so option behavior is not preserved for the new API contractually intended path its own option type and duplicate behavior machinery diverges from repository patterns. may produce inconsistent request semantics compared with Add; for example query options available through FilesOption cannot be used. tests do not cover source-reader errors. It also broadens raw retry machinery beyond the focused Upload implementation."],"risks_b":["Upload also has the wrong ...UploadFileOption signature and bypasses FilesService.Add.","It adds prohibited association fields plus an arbitrary WithFileFormField escape hatch, substantially exceeding scope.","It changes the existing option implementation and exported constructor return types despite the requirement to keep FilesOption behavior unchanged, and still fails to accept arbitrary FilesOption values in Upload. Its additional query/form/request option machinery increases maintenance burden. seekability helper probes SeekEnd, changes Content-Length behavior globally, and may corrupt the initial body position if SeekEnd fails after moving the reader; the comment claiming failed seeks leave offsets untouched is not generally valid. Upload retry test does not use a non-seekable streamed source, and no source-reader error test is present."]}
